overview_markdown:
LettaBot was a personal AI assistant built on the Letta Code SDK that unified conversations across Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, and Signal into a single agent with persistent, cross-session memory. It also supported Bluesky Jetstream feed ingestion, voice message transcription via Whisper, heartbeat check-ins, agent-created reminders and recurring tasks, and local tool execution (file reads, code search, shell commands) on the host machine.

Architecturally, it acted as a multi-channel gateway in front of the Letta platform, requiring either a Letta cloud API key or a self-hosted Letta Docker server. Configuration was YAML-driven, and the codebase was explicitly designed to be 'hackable' by AI coding agents. Deployment was streamlined via a Railway template.

The project is now **officially deprecated and archived**. Letta directs all users to Letta Code's Channels (for messaging), Remote Environments (for always-on agents via outbound WebSocket), and `letta cron` (for scheduling), with a stated ~20-minute migration path. Compared to OpenClaw, LettaBot offered stronger managed-memory infrastructure but weaker local-first posture, a smaller ecosystem, and — decisively — no ongoing maintenance. New users should not adopt it.
